notes: Food isn't taxed, since Delaware has no sales tax. Grocery supermarkets pay a 0.3267% gross receipts tax on what they sell, which isn't charged to shoppers as a tax and isn't counted here.

Restaurant meals aren't taxed: Delaware has no sales or meals tax, and no town meals tax was found. Restaurants pay a 0.6472% gross receipts tax on their sales, which isn't charged to diners as a tax and isn't counted here.

Alcohol pays no tax at the register; excise taxes paid by importers and brewers are left out here: beer $8.15 a barrel (about 26 cents a gallon), cider 27 cents a gallon, wine $1.63 a gallon and spirits $4.50 a gallon ($3.00 at 25% alcohol or less).

Cigarettes pay $2.10 a pack of 20 (105 mills a cigarette), other tobacco 30% of the wholesale price, moist snuff 92 cents an ounce and vapor products 5 cents a milliliter; left out here. A 2026 bill to raise the cigarette tax to $3.60 a pack (House Substitute 1 for House Bill 215) was reported out of committee on April 22, 2026 but died when the session ended June 30, 2026.
Household supplies: diapers and other household supplies aren't taxed, since Delaware has no sales tax.
Personal care products: menstrual products, soap and cosmetics aren't taxed, since Delaware has no sales tax.
Barber and beauty services: haircuts and salon services aren't taxed; businesses selling services pay a 0.3983% gross receipts tax, not charged to customers as a tax and not counted here.
Clothing and shoes aren't taxed; retailers pay a 0.7468% gross receipts tax on their sales, which isn't charged to shoppers as a tax and isn't counted here.
Laundry and dry cleaning aren't taxed; businesses selling services pay a 0.3983% gross receipts tax, not charged to customers as a tax and not counted here.
Gasoline pays 23 cents a gallon (unchanged since January 1, 1995) and diesel 22 cents, left out here.
Repair labor and parts aren't taxed. Buying a vehicle carries the Division of Motor Vehicles' 5.25% document fee (4.25% before October 1, 2025), which isn't counted here.

Hotel stays pay the state's 8% lodging tax and short-term rentals 4.5% (on rentals booked from January 1, 2025); Sussex County adds 3% on hotels outside its towns, New Castle County 3% on hotels outside its towns, and many towns add lodging or rental taxes of their own (Dover 3% since July 1, 2024, was 1.5%; Newark 3%; Milford and Georgetown 3% on hotels since 2019 and Smyrna since July 1, 2022; Millsboro 3% on hotels, enacted June 1, 2026; Wilmington 2%; Lewes 0.5% on hotels in 2026, rising to 2% in 2028, and a 5% tax on other rentals, 5.5% on short-term rentals; Rehoboth Beach 3% on hotels and 7% on rentals (6% earlier; the city's page gives no date for the change); Dewey Beach 3% on hotels and 3% on rentals; Bethany Beach 7% and South Bethany 8% on rentals; Fenwick Island 4% on hotels and 7.5% on every other rental, whatever its length (Code 146-4 as amended October 23, 2026, whose text gives no effective date; hotels 3.5% and short-term rentals 8% before January 1, 2026); Millville 2% on hotels and 2% on rents; Ocean View 6% (5% before 2025) and Selbyville 2% (since January 1, 2025) on all rents, homes and commercial space included; Dagsboro 3% on rents; Henlopen Acres 6.5% on rents); none is counted here. Harrington may levy a lodging tax under a 2025 change to its charter, but none was found. Milton, Slaughter Beach, Laurel, Seaford, Bridgeville, Middletown, Clayton, Camden, Felton, Elsmere, Newport and Delaware City haven't yet been checked for lodging or rental taxes of their own.
Adult-use marijuana pays a 15% state tax since legal sales began on August 1, 2025 (medical marijuana is exempt, and counties and towns may not add their own); not counted here.
Electricity and piped gas pay a 4.25% public utility tax, phone service 5% and cable and satellite TV 2.125%; vehicle leases pay a 1.9914% use tax. None is counted here.
gaps: Delaware has no sales tax, state or local, so no sales-tax revenue is at stake. Sellers pay a gross receipts tax on what they take in instead (0.7468% for most retailers, 0.6472% for restaurants and 0.3267% for grocery supermarkets, after a monthly deduction; 30 Del. C. 2905, 2906, 2908), which isn't charged to shoppers as a tax and isn't counted here.

programs: Downtown Development Districts are mapped from Delaware FirstMap's layer (12 districts); the state rebates up to 20% of qualified construction costs in a district. On October 1, 2026 the Governor designated three more, Claymont, Newport and Millsboro, bringing the program to the 15 the law allows; their boundaries aren't final, so they aren't mapped here. Delaware on Main Street (Division of Small Business) recognizes 17 downtown programs, with no map: accredited are Downtown Wilmington Visions, Cornerstone West CDC (Wilmington), Downtown Dover Partnership, Downtown Milford, Rehoboth Beach Main Street and Middletown Main Street; affiliates are Harrington, Seaford, Clayton, Delaware City, Laurel, Millsboro, Milton, Newark (The Newark Partnership), Elsmere, Smyrna and Georgetown (June 30, 2026). Delaware law allows tax increment financing and special development districts (22 Del. C. ch. 17 and 18; for New Castle County, 9 Del. C. ch. 32 and 33), but no map or list of districts was found. Wilmington's Downtown and Riverfront business improvement districts are mapped from the city's layers (the Downtown boundary last edited in November 2017, the Riverfront's in January 2026).

warn.text: Dover draws many visitors (Dover Motor Speedway, its casino hotel and the state capital), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy over the city as a whole: {visitor_why}. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

Leipsic's page is built from the census tract that covers Kent County's Delaware Bay shore, which it shares with Bowers and parts of Little Creek, Frederica, Dover and Milford. The tract's seasonal homes (316 of 2,019, 15.7%) all lie outside Leipsic, which has none (2020 Census); the tract takes in beach communities such as Bowers Beach, Kitts Hummock and Pickering Beach, and has 1 lodging place, so read that caution with care.

Frankford's visitor caution draws on the seasonal homes in its census tract (292 of 1,489, 19.6%), which takes in the countryside around the town; the 2020 Census counts 5 of them in Frankford itself, so about 287 lie outside the town, and the tract has no lodging places, so read that caution with care.

Lewes' page is built from two census tracts that hold 2,822 of its 3,303 residents (2020 census), the second shared with the area around it; both are flagged as visitor economies on their own, with 15.9% and 13.3% of their homes seasonal.
